verdicts.name: services/config/config_service.py:1264 process_config_form
verdicts.reason: Pure delegation to ConfigFormParserService.process_config_form, which is not in source/; the wrapper itself has nothing to check.

findings.trigger: config.json exists but cannot be parsed or read (a hand-edit with a syntax error, or a root-owned file after a 'docker exec' as root - both have happened in this project). Any caller then does a targeted write: update_config_fields({...}) (e.g. DDC_ADMIN_PASSWORD at start via change_web_ui_password, or a 'version seen' marker) or save_config(partial). _load_json_file (:760) NEVER raises - it logs, records a read error and returns the default {} - so 'existing' is {} at :562 and :431. update_config_fields then calls save_config({<only the updates>}); save_config's Critical Field Protection loop finds nothing in 'existing' to preserve and the atomic rename REPLACES config.json with just the updated keys. bot_token, guild_id, web_ui_password_hash, channel_permissions, language, timezone - all gone, and the method returns success=True / 'Configuration saved successfully'. In the corrupt-JSON case the .json.bak still holds the broken original (recoverable by hand); in the unreadable-file case shutil.copy2 fails too (:464, a warning) and the old inode is renamed away - nothing is left. The 'except (IOError, OSError, ValueError)' branches at :436 and :568, which claim to handle exactly this, are dead code because _load_json_file swallows every error. The docstring of update_config_fields promises 'preventing accidental loss of unrelated fields' - the opposite happens in precisely the state where the protection matters.
findings.suggestion: For the two read-modify-write paths, read config.json with a strict loader that raises (or check that _record_read_error did not fire for main_config_file during the read) and abort with success=False instead of writing. Alternatively: if the file exists but 'existing' came back as {} with a recorded read error, refuse to save.

findings.trigger: config.json holds the bot token in PLAINTEXT. Two paths in this file create that state: (a) _repair_bot_token :917-921 deliberately writes the decrypted copy into 'bot_token' when no web_ui_password_hash exists ('keeping the last decrypted copy so the bot can still log in'); (b) _keep_bot_token_encrypted :883 returns early when 'existing' has no bot_token yet (fresh config.json) or when the old token was already plain, so a plaintext token arriving at save_config is written as-is even when a password hash is present. Now the operator sets a password (panel /setup or DDC_ADMIN_PASSWORD): change_web_ui_password only re-encrypts when the stored token does NOT look like a Discord token (:611), so the plaintext token is skipped; the following save_config sees new_token == old_token (:883) and returns. Result: the bot token stays in plaintext in config.json and in config.json.bak indefinitely, although a key to encrypt it now exists, the bot works, the log says 'Web UI password changed' - nobody notices. Z9 ('never lies on disk in plain text') is contradicted, and the 'Plaintext Token Protection' header at :445 promises more than the narrower docstring at :880 delivers.
findings.suggestion: In change_web_ui_password: if the stored token looks like a Discord token, encrypt it with new_hash and include it in 'updates'. In _keep_bot_token_encrypted: encrypt ANY plaintext bot_token whenever a password hash is available, not only when it replaces an encrypted one. Whether path (b) is reachable depends on the form parser / setup handler encrypting before save - not visible here.

findings.trigger: config.json is unreadable (the state _record_read_error exists for: the panel must not treat it as a fresh install). Two threads call get_config with the cache invalid at the same time - web request plus the bot's status loop, both reload constantly while a directory mtime keeps changing. Thread A sets self._read_errors = [] (:351), loads, records the error; thread B then executes :351 and wipes the list; A reaches :374, sees an empty list, and returns/caches a config WITHOUT 'config_read_errors'. For that request auth.py (per the docstring at :741-747) sees no password hash and no read error and lets admin/setup in. The class docstring says 'All public methods are thread-safe'; get_config holds no lock and shares this instance attribute.
findings.suggestion: Use a local list for the load: pass a collector into the loader/_load_json_file, or hold a lock around the load, or store the errors in a thread-local. Do not reset shared instance state at the start of an unlocked method.
findings.unsure_why: How auth.py consumes 'config_read_errors' and how often two loads overlap in practice is outside source/; the race itself is visible.

findings.trigger: One file in config/containers/ whose top level is not a JSON object - e.g. 'null', a number, or a string (a truncated hand-edit or a stray file). json.load succeeds, then 'container_name' in container_data at :65 raises TypeError (for null/number), or :66/:73 raise TypeError for a list. TypeError is caught neither by the per-file handlers (:99-105) nor by the outer handler (:127), so _load_container_configs raises and get_all_servers / get_ordered_servers / get_server_by_docker_name all fail for EVERY container. The comment at :107-121 promises the opposite: an unreadable file removes only that container and says so once.
findings.suggestion: After json.load, check isinstance(container_data, dict); if not, append to 'unreadable' with an error and continue. Also add ValueError/TypeError/UnicodeDecodeError to the per-file handler so one bad file cannot take the whole list down.

findings.trigger: A v1.1.x monolithic config.json with the legacy channel format - 'channels' as an ARRAY of {channel_id, permissions:[...]} - which is exactly the 'old format fallback' that channel_roles.py:31-37 still reads. extract_channels_config keeps 'channels' only if it is a dict, otherwise {} - so the legacy list is silently replaced by an empty dict when this extractor is used by the v1 migration (config_service.py:1045). The two places disagree about what the old format looks like.
findings.suggestion: Accept a list for 'channels' (convert to the new channel_permissions form, or pass it through) or make the migration service read config['channels'] directly; either way the two readers of the old format must agree.
findings.unsure_why: ConfigMigrationService.migrate_legacy_v1_config_if_needed is not in source/; it may take the channel list from the raw config instead of from this extractor.

findings.trigger: A legacy config.json with a non-numeric 'session_timeout' string (e.g. '1h' or '') - int('1h') raises ValueError, the except at :129 returns get_default_web_config() and thereby drops web_ui_password_hash (None), donation_disable_key and advanced_settings for the whole web section. Used by the v1 migration (config_service.py:1044), the migrated install lands in first-run setup mode (admin/setup accepted everywhere, see config_service.py:744-746) with only a warning in the log.
findings.suggestion: Convert field by field with per-field fallback (session_timeout -> 3600 on ValueError) instead of replacing the whole section; never let one bad field discard the password hash.
findings.unsure_why: Only reachable through the v1 migration path, which is not in source/; whether it validates before calling this extractor is unknown.

findings.trigger: The operator types a game-query port of 70000 (or 'abc'), or an unsupported protocol string: the port becomes 0 (= auto-discover) and the protocol 'source', silently; the panel reports the container as saved. Later queries go to a different target than configured while the settings look accepted. The project's own principle, stated in this section at config_service.py:1122-1124, is that silently clamping 'would tell the user saved while pricing differently' - this sanitizer does exactly that.
findings.suggestion: Return or raise a validation error for out-of-range port / unknown protocol so the form can refuse the save, or at least return a list of corrections the caller must show.
findings.unsure_why: The form/JS layer may validate before calling this; the docstring calls the clamping intended, but no B-decision in SPEC.md covers it.

findings.trigger: save_config receives a value json.dump cannot serialize (a datetime, set or Path slipped into the config dict by a caller). json.dump at :480 raises TypeError inside the inner try, whose except catches only (IOError, OSError), so the temp file '.config_XXXX.json.tmp' is NOT removed; the outer except at :534 raises ConfigSaveError. Every such attempt leaves another temp file in config/ and bumps the directory mtime (which drives cache invalidation).
findings.suggestion: Make the inner cleanup 'except Exception: unlink temp; raise' like _save_json_file at :813 does.

findings.trigger: evolution_mode.json hand-edited to {"use_dynamic": "false", ...}: the string is truthy, so the mech stays on dynamic pricing while the file says static. difficulty_multiplier was given a read-side bounds check for exactly this file (:136-153); use_dynamic was not.
findings.suggestion: Coerce use_dynamic with the same care: accept only bool (or recognised strings), otherwise log and fall back to True.

findings.trigger: channel_permissions with a non-dict entry, e.g. {"123": {"commands": null}} or {"123": []}: (perms or {}).get('commands', {}) returns None (key present, value null) and .get('control') raises AttributeError. status_channel_ids (:49-51) guards both shapes with isinstance; control_channel_ids does not. The update notice and the watchdog default-channel lookup (the two named callers) crash instead of skipping the entry.
findings.suggestion: Apply the same isinstance guards as status_channel_ids, or share one helper for both.
findings.unsure_why: Whether the channel loader can ever deliver a non-dict 'commands' value is outside source/.

findings.trigger: A config still in the old format (channels array with 'serverstatus' in permissions, no channel_permissions dict): control_channel_ids finds the control channels via its old-format fallback (:31-38), but status_channel_ids has no such fallback and returns [] - the donation appeal, member count and player warning have no channel to post in, without any error.
findings.suggestion: Either add the same old-format fallback to status_channel_ids or drop it from control_channel_ids so the two answer the same question the same way.
findings.unsure_why: Whether an old-format config can still exist at runtime after the migrations is outside source/.

notes: Module-level save_config (:1240) and update_config_fields (:1245) are documented as returning bool, but ConfigService.save_config raises ConfigSaveError on every failure, so the wrappers never return False - a caller written against the bool contract gets an exception instead (loud, so not a finding; callers not visible). change_web_ui_password reads old_hash/stored_token outside _save_lock (:606-609) and writes inside it - two concurrent password changes could re-encrypt with a stale hash; too rare to state a clean trigger. change_web_ui_password also reports success when the stored token cannot be decrypted with the old hash (:620-625) - the token was unusable before, so nothing new is lost, but the operator is not told at the moment of the change. save_config's _critical_fields (:425) names 'encrypted_bot_token', while extract_bot_config (:95) uses 'bot_token_encrypted' - the two key spellings never meet; probably harmless drift. Critical Field Protection preserves only fields ABSENT from main_config; an explicit empty value (bot_token: '' or channel_permissions: {}) erases the stored one - the spec test cited at :425 seems to intend this, and B8 places the 'empty means keep' rule in the form parser, which is not in source/. sanitize_query_config keeps 'host:port' in the host when the scheme is stripped (:66-68) - the consumer is not visible. ServerConfigService and ConfigLoaderService (get_config()['servers']) both load container JSONs with their own defaults (allowed_actions ['status'], order 999, active True) - a second implementation that can drift; the loader is not in source/. ContainerConfigSaveService writes into config/containers/ - whether ConfigCacheService's directory-mtime check notices a write in the subdirectory (and so refreshes get_config()['servers']) is not visible. ConfigService sets _initialized = True (:265) before ensure_modular_structure and the legacy fold run; if the first raised, the half-built singleton would be returned afterwards - no trigger stated because the migration service is not visible. get_evolution_mode_service records a read error into self._read_errors for a broken evolution_mode.json (:1186 via _load_json_file); if that coincides with a running get_config load, a mech settings file could lock the panel login for one load - noted, not filed.
